# Menus and keyboard shortcuts

This page lists every command in Frame Job's menu bar, in menu order, with
its shortcut. After the menus come the keys that work without a menu item,
the mouse and trackpad gestures on the timeline and the preview canvas, and
the context menus you get with a right-click. Each entry says in a few words
what the command does. The page that covers the feature explains it in full.

Symbols: ⌘ Command, ⌥ Option, ⇧ Shift, ⌃ Control, ⌫ Delete, ↩ Return,
⎋ Escape, ← → ↑ ↓ the arrow keys.

## How the keys are shared

- **Single-letter keys** (Space, J, K, L, I, O, M, W, E, T, C, Z, N, `,`, `.`)
  and the arrow keys belong to the editor window. They don't work while you
  are typing in a field, and they don't work while a sheet is open. Some
  menu items also have a single-letter key. The menu doesn't show those
  letters, so this page gives them in the menu tables as "(key)".
- **⌘ shortcuts** are menu shortcuts. A shortcut does nothing when its menu
  item is greyed out.
- **Delete (⌫), ⌘⌫, ⌘↓ and ⌘↑** are switched off while you type in a text
  field. In a field they keep their usual text-editing meaning.
- In a sheet, ↩ presses the default button and ⎋ cancels.
- macOS may add some items of its own to these menus. Those items are not
  listed here.

## Frame Job menu

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| About Frame Job | | The version and credits panel |
| Check for Updates… | | Asks whether a newer Frame Job has been published, and offers to install it. Only in the copy you download from GitHub; a build from source has no updater ([Settings](settings.md#updates)) |
| Settings… | ⌘, | Opens the Settings window ([Settings](settings.md)) |
| Hide Frame Job | ⌘H | Hides the app |
| Hide Others | ⌥⌘H | Hides every other app |
| Show All | | Shows hidden apps again |
| Quit Frame Job | ⌘Q | Quits |

## File menu

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| New Project | ⌘N | A new, empty project window |
| New Recording… | ⌥⌘N | Opens the recorder. While a recording runs, the item is called **Stop Recording** and stops it ([Screen recording](screen-recording.md)) |
| Pause Recording | | Pauses the running recording. It is called **Resume Recording** while paused, and is enabled only during a recording |
| New Project from Range… | | Opens the In–Out range as a new untitled project, with its media's caches and its graphics ([New Project from Range](projects-and-media.md#new-project-from-range)). Enabled with an In–Out range set and no nest open |
| Make Vertical Version… | | Makes a 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1 version of the timeline, each full-frame movie clip following its subject — with Follow Speaker, a wide shot of two to four people cutting to whoever is talking on the microphones you tick — opened as a new untitled project or made in this one ([Make Vertical Version](vertical-and-framing.md#make-vertical-version)) |
| Open… | ⌘O | Opens a project or a media file |
| Open Recent ▸ | | Recently opened documents, then **Clear Menu** |
| Close | ⌘W | Closes the window |
| Save | ⌘S | Saves the project |
| Duplicate | ⇧⌘S | Opens a copy of the project as a new, untitled document. Hold ⌥ and the item becomes **Save As…** (⌥⇧⌘S), which writes the project to a new package |
| Rename… | | Renames the project's package |
| Move To… | | Moves the project's package to another folder |
| Revert To ▸ | | Goes back to the last saved version, or browses earlier versions of the package |
| Share | | The macOS Share menu for the project |
| Add Media… | ⇧⌘I | Imports files into the project's Media list ([Projects and media](projects-and-media.md)) |
| Import Captions… | | Reads a caption file onto a caption track ([Captions](captions.md)) |
| Generate Captions… | | Makes captions from speech |
| Export Captions… | | Writes a caption track out as a file |
| Re-lay Captions for This Canvas | | Re-pages the word caption tracks for the current canvas, every correction kept ([Captions](captions.md#re-lay-captions-for-a-new-canvas)) |
| Consolidate Media… | | Copies the project's media into the project package |
| Add Font to Graphics… | | Adds a font that graphics can use ([Graphics](graphics.md)) |
| Add Image to Graphics… | | Adds a picture that graphics can use |
| Rename Graphic… | | Renames one of the project's graphics. Greyed when the project has no graphics, or while a nest is open |
| Delete Graphic… | | Deletes a graphic that no clip uses |
| Restore Graphic Version… | | Brings back an earlier version of a graphic |
| Export… | ⌘E | The export sheet ([Export](export.md)) |
| Save Frame… | ⌥⌘E | Saves the frame under the playhead as a PNG, JPEG or HEIC still |

*Agents:* `new_project`, `open_project`, `save_project`, `close_project`,
`import_media`, `import_captions`, `transcribe`, `export_captions`, `relay_captions`,
`consolidate_media`, `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset`,
`rename_graphic`, `delete_graphic`, `restore_graphic`, `export`,
`render_frame` (Save Frame…'s writer) and `record_screen`.

### When File items are available

| Item | Enabled when |
|---|---|
| Make Vertical Version… | The project has a clip, no nest is open and no recording is running |
| Generate Captions… | Some clip plays sound from a media file forwards, with its audio on |
| Export Captions… | The project has a caption track: a track whose clips are all text clips |
| Re-lay Captions for This Canvas | The timeline (or the open nest) has a word caption track Frame Job can re-lay, no sheet is open and no recording is running |
| Consolidate Media… | The project has media |
| Rename Graphic… | The project has graphics and no nest is open |
| Delete Graphic… | The project has graphics |
| Restore Graphic Version… | An earlier version of a graphic is kept |
| Export…, Save Frame… | The project is not empty |

## Edit menu

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Undo | ⌘Z | Undoes the last edit. The item names it, for example **Undo Move Clips** or **Undo Ripple Delete** |
| Redo | ⇧⌘Z | Redoes it, named the same way |
| Cut | ⌘X | Cuts the selected clips |
| Copy | ⌘C | Copies the selected clips |
| Paste | ⌘V | Pastes clips at the playhead. Nothing needs to be selected |
| Paste Attributes | ⌥⌘V | Puts the copied clip's look onto the selected clips |
| Paste Graphic Properties | | Puts the copied graphic's properties onto the selected clips that use the same graphic |
| Duplicate | ⌘D | Copies the selected clips and places the copies after them |
| Delete | ⌫ | Removes the selection and leaves a gap. With nothing selected it lifts the in/out range. With an action selected it removes that action |
| Ripple Delete | ⌘⌫ | Removes the selection, or the in/out range when nothing is selected, and closes the gap |
| Insert at Playhead | | Inserts the file selected in the Media tab, pushing later clips along |
| Overwrite at Playhead | | Places that file over whatever is already there |
| Select All | ⌘A | Selects every clip |
| Select After Playhead | ⌥⌘A | Selects every clip that starts at or after the playhead |
| Select All on Track | | Selects every clip on the current track |

Cut and Copy need a selection. Paste needs copied clips on the clipboard.
Paste Attributes needs copied clips and a selection. Paste Graphic
Properties needs copied clips and a selected graphic clip. Insert and
Overwrite at Playhead are enabled only while a file is selected in the Media
tab, and never for a LUT. Select All on Track needs a current track and a
timeline with clips. The *current track* is the track of the
first selected clip. With nothing selected it is the front-most track. See
[Editing](editing.md).

*Agents:* `undo`, `redo`, `paste`, `paste_attributes`, `duplicate`, `delete`,
`lift_range`, `ripple_delete`, `ripple_delete_range`, `insert_clip`,
`overwrite_clip`, `set_selection`.

## Insert menu

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Adjustment Clip | | Adds an adjustment clip over the in/out range. Without a range it covers the selected clips' span, and without a selection the whole timeline. Greyed while a nest is open ([Colour grading](color-grading.md)) |
| Graphic… | | Opens the Graphic dialog: the bundled templates by category (and This Project's own graphics), a looping preview, and Insert to add the chosen one at the playhead, From File… to add a `.js` file or import a `.fjgraphic` you choose, or Export… to save the chosen one as a `.fjgraphic` file ([Graphics](graphics.md#adding-a-graphic)) |
| Text Behind Subject | | Puts a title on a new track above the camera clip at the playhead, behind the person, for 4 s or the clip's rest; turns Remove Background on with Keep background when the clip has none ([Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md#text-behind-the-subject)) |

*Agents:* `add_adjustment_clip`; `list_graphics` and `insert_graphic`, or
`write_graphic` followed by `add_graphic_clip`; `text_behind_subject`.

## Clip menu

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Split | ⌘T | Cuts the selected clips at the playhead. With nothing selected, it cuts every clip under the playhead |
| Split at Shot Changes | — | Cuts each selected clip of a video file at every hard cut inside it, as one undo step. The Analyzing sheet shows while the cuts are found on this Mac ([Editing](editing.md#split-at-shot-changes)) |
| Trim Start to Playhead | W (key) | Trims the selected clips' starts to the playhead |
| Trim End to Playhead | E (key) | Trims their ends to the playhead |
| Freeze Frame | ⇧⌘F | Holds the frame under the playhead as a still clip |
| Detach Audio | ⌥⌘D | Moves a clip's sound onto its own clip, linked to it ([Audio](audio.md)) |
| Attach Audio | ⇧⌥⌘D | Merges a detached sound back into its picture ([Audio](audio.md#attach-audio)) |
| Normalize | | Sets the selected clips' volume to a loudness (the default, turning a clip's limiter on when its peaks need it) or a peak, by the mode chosen in the Volume section's Normalize row. A clip with processing is measured through it under the Measuring Sound sheet |
| Enhance Voice | | Sets the selected clips up for speech from their own measurements: high-pass, isolation or noise reduction and a gate for noisy pauses, the leveller for an uneven voice, the de-esser, a compressor, the limiter and the volume to the Normalize row's target ([Audio](audio.md#enhance-voice)) |
| Match Audio… | | Gives the selected clips the loudness and the speech's tone of one of them, chosen in a sheet: their volume and limiter, and their EQ's shelves and bands, measured under the Measuring Sound sheet ([Audio](audio.md#match-audio)) |
| Synchronize Audio | | Lines up the selected clips by their sound. Needs two or more clips that play sound |
| Switch by Speaker… | | Cuts a Program track from the selected cameras, showing whoever talks on each microphone, as one undo step; run Synchronize Audio first ([Podcasts and several cameras](multicam.md#switch-by-speaker)) |
| Add Action | ⌥⌘K | Adds an action at the playhead ([Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md)) |
| Auto Zoom… | | Zooms the selected screen recordings in at their clicks and typing and back out after, as ordinary actions, in one undo step ([Screen recording](screen-recording.md#auto-zoom)) |
| Follow Subject… | | Frames each selected movie clip on its subject — faces, people or the region the eye goes to, found on this Mac — with eased moves on its action lane and a blurred copy on a Backgrounds track where it shows the whole picture, in one undo step ([Vertical and framing](vertical-and-framing.md#follow-subject)) |
| Add Shortcut Overlays | | Shows each keyboard shortcut recorded in the selected screen recordings as keycaps at the moment it was pressed, on a "Shortcuts" track, in one undo step ([Screen recording](screen-recording.md#shortcut-overlays)) |
| Speed Up Typing… | | Plays the typing in the selected screen recordings faster where nobody speaks and no shortcut shows, in one undo step ([Screen recording](screen-recording.md#speeding-up-typing)) |
| Speed… | | Sets the selected clips' playback rate ([Speed](speed.md)) |
| Speed Ramp… | | Puts a speed ramp preset on one selected media clip |
| Close Gap | | Closes the gap under the playhead on the current track |
| Retime Range… | | Plays the In–Out range faster or slower on every unlocked track and moves what follows to stay in step ([Speed](speed.md#retime-a-range)) |
| Remove Silences… | | Finds silent stretches and removes them ([Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md)) |
| Remove Filler Words… | | Finds "um"s and "uh"s and removes them |
| Transition ▸ | | Sets the transition into the clip |
| Motion ▸ | | Sets how the clip enters, leaves and moves |
| Look ▸ | | Puts a look or a LUT on the clip ([Colour grading](color-grading.md)) |
| Remove Background | | Keeps the person and removes the rest of the picture, or turns that off; checked when every selected clip has it, a dash when some do ([Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md#remove-background)) |
| Camera Layout ▸ | | Lays out the camera and the screen behind it at the playhead — Corner ▸, Rounded Corner ▸ or Circle ▸ (each Bottom Right, Bottom Left, Top Right, Top Left), Side by Side, Stacked, Camera Full or Screen Only — eased over half a second and held until the next switch; the crop centred on the person when the camera's masks are cached; a zoom in the way offers Nest and Switch ([Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md#camera-layouts)) |
| Switch Angle ▸ | | Re-picks the selected shot from another camera track that covers it, keeping its span, its switches and its dissolves, as one undo step; the new pieces are selected ([Podcasts and several cameras](multicam.md)) |
| Add Background ▸ Solid Color | | Puts a colour plate on a new track behind everything ([Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md)) |
| Add Background ▸ Image… | | Puts a picture you choose on a new track behind everything |
| Add Blurred Background | | Puts a blurred copy of the picture on a new track behind everything |
| Rename… | ⇧⌘R | Renames the selected clip in place on the timeline |
| Label ▸ | | Gives the clip a colour label |
| Nest | ⌘G | Wraps the selected clips into one nest clip |
| Un-nest | ⇧⌘G | Breaks a nest clip back into its clips |
| Open Nest | ⌘↓ | Goes inside the selected nest clip |
| Close Nest | ⌘↑ | Comes back out by one level |

### Clip submenus

- **Transition ▸**: Cross Dissolve, Fade Through Black, Fade Through White,
  Push Left, Push Right, Push Up, Push Down, Wipe, Slide, Zoom, Wipe Left,
  Wipe Up, Wipe Down, then **None**. A checkmark shows the selected clip's
  transition. A transition can be picked only on a clip that has room for
  one. **None** works for any selection, so a stored transition can always
  be cleared.
- **Motion ▸ In ▸** and **Motion ▸ Out ▸**: Fade, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Slide
  Left, Slide Right, Slide Up, Slide Down, Spin, Pop, then **None**.
- **Motion ▸ During ▸**: Pulse, Shake, Spin, Bounce, Drift, then **None**.
- In each Motion submenu a checkmark shows the kind every selected clip
  has. An In or Out kind whose length is zero reads **\<Kind\> (inactive)**,
  or **(some inactive)** when only some of the selected clips with that kind
  have zero length.
- **Motion ▸ Preview**: sets the in/out range to the clip, turns Loop on and
  plays it. The range and Loop stay set afterwards.
- **Look ▸**: Warm, Cool, Teal & Orange, Vivid, Faded, Vintage, Dramatic,
  Black & White. Then come the project's `.cube` LUTs, when it has any, and
  then **None**. A checkmark marks a look that every selected clip has. A
  dash marks one that only some of them have.
- **Label ▸**: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Purple (each shown with its
  colour dot), then **None**. A checkmark shows the label the selected clips

Once a project has been saved it autosaves in place, the macOS way: changes are written to the package as you work, and the package is written beside the old one and swapped in, so a crash part-way through a save cannot leave half a package behind. Because of this, macOS adds its standard document commands to the File menu: **Duplicate**, **Rename…**, **Move To…**, **Revert To ▸** (in place of Revert to Saved) and **Share**, and the same Rename and Move To controls appear when you click the window's title. A project only ever saves as a `.framejob` package. Making a movie or a still is a separate step; see [Export](export.md).

*Agents:* `save_project` (a `path` is required the first time and always means Save As), `close_project` (refused when `get_project` reports `unsaved_changes` unless `discard: true`, and refused while a sheet is open), `get_project` (the whole project as JSON plus the playhead, selection, in/out range, `unsaved_changes` and `missing_media`). `new_project` adds `.framejob` to a `path` that lacks it. `new_project` and `save_project` refuse a path another open project holds (close that one first) or one a window is still opening.

## What a `.framejob` package holds

A package is a folder that the Finder shows as one file:

| Inside | What it is |
|---|---|
| `project.json` | The edit itself: canvas, media list, tracks, clips, markers. The only thing a package needs in order to open. |
| `cache/` | Things Frame Job can rebuild: filmstrip thumbnails, waveforms, the voice-detection and sync analyses, transcripts, reversed clips, speed-ramp audio, the shot changes, faces, sound events and subjects (people and salient regions) found for an agent, the faces and subjects drawn by View ▸ Show Subjects, and the person masks found for one or made for a clip with Remove Background (`cache/analysis/`; a minute of 1080p video's masks take about 62 MB). A package with a missing or damaged `cache/` still opens and just redraws. |
| `media/` | Only after **Consolidate Media…**: copies of the footage (see [Consolidate Media](#consolidate-media)). |
| `graphics/` | Only once you add a graphic: graphic modules, their fonts, images and kept versions. See [Graphics](graphics.md). |

**Media is referenced, not copied.** By default a project remembers where each file lives (its path and a Finder bookmark, so a moved file is often found again) and reads it from there. The package stays small, but it depends on the footage staying put. Consolidate Media is how you make a package hold everything it needs.

Caches are built in the background after an open, an import or a relink, and the timeline fills in as they finish. Frame Job builds at most two files' sound caches at a time, on threads of their own, so importing many long files at once does not hold up playback or a speed ramp's sound. A cache that already matches its file is never rebuilt. Moving, copying or consolidating the package keeps its caches. Until an untitled project is first saved, its caches live in a temporary folder; the first save copies them in.

*Transcripts* cost money to rebuild when they came from the cloud engine, so treat `cache/transcripts/` as worth keeping. See [Captions](captions.md).

## The Document tab: canvas settings

The canvas is the fixed frame every clip is composited into, and every export starts from its size. It is set on the inspector's **Document** tab, in five sections. Every change there to the project is one undo step (**Resize clips proportionally** is a preference on this Mac, not part of the project, so it is not undone).

### Document (summary)


### What Frame Job reads

| Kind | Files |
|---|---|
| Movies | MOV, MP4, M4V and other containers macOS plays: H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG and MPEG-4 video; VP9 Profile 0 and 2 in MP4; AV1 on an M3 or later Mac. |
| WebM and Matroska | `.webm` and `.mkv` with VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC video and Opus, Vorbis or AAC sound (see below). |
| Sound | M4A (AAC, ALAC), MP3, WAV and AIFF everywhere. Other formats macOS plays, such as CAF and FLAC, import when dropped on the Media tab. |
| Pictures | PNG, JPEG and HEIC everywhere. TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP also import when dropped on the Media tab. |
| LUTs | `.cube` 3D LUTs, applied as a clip's look or as a file's Camera Log. See [Color grading](color-grading.md). |

Caption files (`.srt`) are not media: bring them in with **File ▸ Import Captions…**. See [Captions](captions.md).

### Add Media

**File ▸ Add Media…** (⇧⌘I), or the Media tab's **Add Media…** button, opens a panel for one or more files. Every file is checked first. The readable ones are added to the Media tab together as one undo step ("Add Media", or "Add 3 Media Files"). A file that cannot be read shows an alert naming it, and the rest are still added. Adding a file that is already in the list changes nothing.

An agent's import never shows this question. Unless you have chosen "always", the file is refused instead.

### Files that are refused

- **A codec this Mac cannot decode** is refused at import with a sentence naming it, for example "*file* is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac." or "*file* is VP9 Profile 1 video, which this Mac cannot decode; VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import." VP8 is refused the same way. A file in a codec this Mac does decode still imports even when some of its data is damaged.
- **A `.cube` the LUT reader cannot read** is refused naming the line and the problem, for example "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65."
- "Could not read *file*." means the file is damaged or not a format Frame Job reads.
- "*file* has no video or audio the app can open." means the file holds neither.
- "Timed out reading *file*." means the check took longer than 30 seconds, usually because the file is on a stalled network volume.

## The Media tab

The inspector's **Media** tab lists every file the project has imported, in a bar, a find band, the list and a footer.

*Agents:* `consolidate_media` (needs a saved project; can take a while and copies as many bytes as the footage weighs).

## Limits

- Consolidate Media needs a saved project.
- Canvas width and height are even numbers from 16 to 16384 px.
- A project holds at most 4,096 clips and 64 tracks (counting those inside nests), 1,024 markers and 1,024 media files, with nests up to 8 deep.
- The Add Media… and Open panels list movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG, HEIC and (Add Media… only) `.cube`. Other sound and picture formats import only by a drop on the Media tab, or through `import_media`.
- `.cube` files are imported, not opened: File ▸ Open… does not take one, and a `.cube` dropped on the window or the Dock is not imported. Use Add Media… or a drop on the Media tab.
- A project file that is damaged or out of range fails to open with a message naming the problem; the package is not rewritten. A package saved by a newer Frame Job reports "project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it". A package with no readable `project.json` reports "*name* does not contain a readable project.json."
# Frame Job

A screencast video editor. A project is a document of tracks and clips that the core edits through ops; the app and the agent both speak in those ops. This glossary holds the terms the spec and the op table use, sharpened as decisions settle them.

## Language

**Op**:
One edit to a project, named by a row of the op table and applied whole. An op the core understood answers one of exactly three ways: it applies and yields a new project, it is an identity, or it is refused. A request the core could not read at all is none of the three — that is a mistake in the asking rather than an answer about the project.
_Avoid_: command, mutation, action (an action is an animation on a clip)

**Identity**:
An op that was understood and had nothing to change: the project already says what was asked, or the op was handed an empty selection. It leaves the project exactly as it was, makes no undo step, and has nothing to explain — a caller told about a rule here would go looking for one it did not break.
_Avoid_: no-op, failure, "nothing happened" (all three hide the difference from a refusal)

**Refusal**:
A rule declining an op, in that rule's own sentence: which track is locked, which clips still show the media, by how many ticks two clips would overlap and how long the shorter one is. Like an identity it leaves the project exactly as it was and makes no undo step; unlike an identity it says why, and it names what a caller could send instead rather than restating the rule. A refusal is not an error — an error is a request that could not be read.
_Avoid_: error, rejection, failure, "invalid"

**Op table**:
The one list of the ops and their arguments, kept by the core and published by it. A row is an op's name and, per **Argument**, its name, its kind and whether it is required — the STRUCTURE of a call and nothing about its meaning, which stays in the prose beside the ops themselves. Everything downstream — the tool catalog an agent reads, the check that compares the two at startup — reads the table rather than restating it, so an argument is written down once and a row that lies is a failing test rather than a call that goes wrong.
_Avoid_: schema, op list, the op enum (the enum is one implementation of the table)

**Argument**:
One named value an **Op** takes, checked against the op table. An argument is part of the CALL: the core knows what it is — ticks, an id, a boolean, a closed vocabulary — and the app says what it is FOR. Distinct from a **Patch**'s keys, which are part of a VALUE and are checked against the property vocabulary instead: `set_video` takes the two arguments `clips` and `patch`, and everything inside that patch is not an argument at all. A name no tool published is not an argument either: it is refused at the door, naming the tool and what it does take, and never dropped.
_Avoid_: parameter, field, key, option

**Patch**:
A partial object a caller writes to say what to change — a clip's property group, a clip's own name and label, or an action's end state. It merges key by key at every depth; a key set to null clears that key, or removes it from an end state; an array replaces the whole list. A key or value the vocabulary does not have is refused by its dotted path, and never dropped, corrected or clamped. The core is the one that reads it, wherever it came from.
_Avoid_: update, delta, diff, replacement

**Selected action**:
The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing, or none. It is view state, like the playhead and the clip selection: not an edit, not undoable, not saved, and not something an agent sets — an agent names an action by its id. It is chosen by clicking the action's band, or by the playhead ENTERING the action's span; it stays chosen when the playhead leaves, and goes when the clip selection changes, on esc, or on the lane's Clip chip. While one is chosen the fields show and write its END state (spec §11 CI-1, CI-2). Actions are numbered by time order.
_Avoid_: current action, active action, "the action under the playhead" (the playhead no longer decides)

**Graphic**:
A clip whose picture is drawn by code: a **Module** in the package's `graphics/` folder, run per frame with the clip's props, rasterized at the graphic's own size. It is a clip's CONTENT, in the place a media file or an image sits — not an effect, and not a plugin: its code reaches no other clip, no timeline, no model and no file, and the same frame with the same props always draws the same pixels (spec §11 G-1, G-5).
_Avoid_: effect, plugin, overlay, template (a template is a graphic someone else wrote)

**Template**:
A **Module** the app ships, which a person copies into their package with Insert ▸ Graphic…: the file is written into `graphics/` under a free name (`lower-third`, then `lower-third-2`) and a clip drawn by it is placed at the playhead. Once copied it is the package's own module — editing it changes no other package, and no later app version reaches it. Its title in the Graphic dialog is its `meta.name`, read by compiling it once when the dialog first opens, else its file name made a title; the menu bar compiles nothing (spec §11 G-16, G-45).
_Avoid_: preset (a preset is stored settings, not code), sample, built-in graphic

**Category**:
The list a **Module** is filed under in the Graphic dialog: its `meta.category`, else Other. Every bundled **Template** has one of Data & Time, Screencast, Social & YouTube and Titles & Text; the package's own modules are all listed under This Project, first, whatever their own category (spec §11 G-45).
_Avoid_: folder, group, tag

**Graphic package**:
A `.fjgraphic` file the Graphic dialog's Export… writes (`export_graphic` for an agent): a stored zip of a `manifest.json`, one **Module** and only the project fonts and assets the engine was seen to draw, measure, fall back to or resolve while drawing the graphic's frames and its `enum`/boolean variants — never one of the app's bundled fonts. Its paths mirror `graphics/`, so a later import is a copy; a file name the zip path cannot hold is stored under a tidied one, the manifest keeping the original. Exporting is not an edit. Frame Job opens one (a Finder double-click, the Graphic dialog's From File…, `import_graphic`) to import it: checked, asked about, and its files copied into the front project's `graphics/` under the manifest's names (spec §11 G-46, G-47).
_Avoid_: graphic archive, bundle, template file (a **Template** ships with the app)

**Error card**:
What a **Graphic** draws in its own box when it cannot draw itself — its **Module** is missing or does not compile, or a frame throws, runs past its budget or will not rasterize: dark red, a bright red border, and the graphic's name, its frame and the first diagnostic with its line and column in white. Never the last good frame, which would hide the error from someone scrubbing. An export never delivers one: it is refused before it starts, or stopped at the frame, with no file left (spec §11 G-8).
_Avoid_: slate (the slate is what a layer with no source at all draws), error frame, placeholder

**Module**:
A graphic's source: one JavaScript ES module exporting `render(frame, props, ctx)`, which returns SVG, and optionally `meta` and `schema`. It is compiled once and drawn many times; the standard library is global and nothing can be imported. Many clips may name one module, as many clips share one media file.
_Avoid_: script, component, file (the file holds the module), plugin

**Revision**:
Which text of a **Module** drew a frame: the SHA-256 of its source's bytes, 64 hex digits. Two identical texts are one revision wherever they came from; an edit to the file is a new revision, and an export pins the revision it started with.
_Avoid_: version (the font and asset set has a version), hash, edit number

**Kept revision**:
An earlier text of a **Module** the app kept, named by its **Revision**: the text a write replaced while the project was open, or the text a delete removed. The last 10 per module live in the package's `graphics/history/<name>/`, never the current text among them, and move with the module when it is renamed. A name with no file but with kept revisions is a deleted module (spec §11 G-27, G-29).
_Avoid_: backup, snapshot, undo step (restoring one is a file write, not undo), version

**Props**:
The values a **Graphic** is drawn with, stored on its clip in the caller's key order — a title, an accent colour, a size. When the op that sets them carries the module's schema, each is checked by its dotted path (`props.accent`) for its type, its range and its options, and a colour is stored as lowercase hex; without one, only its shape. Distinct from a **Patch**, which is what a caller SENDS to change them: a patch's `props` merges into the stored props key by key, and a null in it removes that key (spec §11 G-4, G-12).
_Avoid_: parameters, inputs, settings, variables

Once a project has been saved it autosaves in place, the macOS way: changes are written to the package as you work, and the package is written beside the old one and swapped in, so a crash part-way through a save cannot leave half a package behind. Because of this, macOS adds its standard document commands to the File menu: **Duplicate**, **Rename…**, **Move To…**, **Revert To ▸** (in place of Revert to Saved) and **Share**, and the same Rename and Move To controls appear when you click the window's title. A project only ever saves as a `.framejob` package. Making a movie or a still is a separate step; see [Export](export.md).

*Agents:* `save_project` (a `path` is required the first time and always means Save As), `close_project` (refused when `get_project` reports `unsaved_changes` unless `discard: true`, and refused while a sheet is open), `get_project` (the whole project as JSON plus the playhead, selection, in/out range, `unsaved_changes` and `missing_media`). `new_project` adds `.framejob` to a `path` that lacks it. `new_project` and `save_project` refuse a path another open project holds (close that one first) or one a window is still opening.

## What a `.framejob` package holds

A package is a folder that the Finder shows as one file:

| Inside | What it is |
|---|---|
| `project.json` | The edit itself: canvas, media list, tracks, clips, markers. The only thing a package needs in order to open. |
| `cache/` | Things Frame Job can rebuild: filmstrip thumbnails, waveforms, the voice-detection and sync analyses, transcripts, reversed clips, speed-ramp audio, the shot changes, faces, sound events and subjects (people and salient regions) found for an agent, the faces and subjects drawn by View ▸ Show Subjects, and the person masks found for one or made for a clip with Remove Background (`cache/analysis/`; a minute of 1080p video's masks take about 62 MB). A package with a missing or damaged `cache/` still opens and just redraws. |
| `media/` | Only after **Consolidate Media…**: copies of the footage (see [Consolidate Media](#consolidate-media)). |
| `graphics/` | Only once you add a graphic: graphic modules, their fonts, images and kept versions. See [Graphics](graphics.md). |

**Media is referenced, not copied.** By default a project remembers where each file lives (its path and a Finder bookmark, so a moved file is often found again) and reads it from there. The package stays small, but it depends on the footage staying put. Consolidate Media is how you make a package hold everything it needs.

Caches are built in the background after an open, an import or a relink, and the timeline fills in as they finish. Frame Job builds at most two files' sound caches at a time, on threads of their own, so importing many long files at once does not hold up playback or a speed ramp's sound. A cache that already matches its file is never rebuilt. Moving, copying or consolidating the package keeps its caches. Until an untitled project is first saved, its caches live in a temporary folder; the first save copies them in.

*Transcripts* cost money to rebuild when they came from the cloud engine, so treat `cache/transcripts/` as worth keeping. See [Captions](captions.md).

## The Document tab: canvas settings

The canvas is the fixed frame every clip is composited into, and every export starts from its size. It is set on the inspector's **Document** tab, in five sections. Every change there to the project is one undo step (**Resize clips proportionally** is a preference on this Mac, not part of the project, so it is not undone).

### Document (summary)


### What Frame Job reads

| Kind | Files |
|---|---|
| Movies | MOV, MP4, M4V and other containers macOS plays: H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG and MPEG-4 video; VP9 Profile 0 and 2 in MP4; AV1 on an M3 or later Mac. |
| WebM and Matroska | `.webm` and `.mkv` with VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC video and Opus, Vorbis or AAC sound (see below). |
| Sound | M4A (AAC, ALAC), MP3, WAV and AIFF everywhere. Other formats macOS plays, such as CAF and FLAC, import when dropped on the Media tab. |
| Pictures | PNG, JPEG and HEIC everywhere. TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP also import when dropped on the Media tab. |
| LUTs | `.cube` 3D LUTs, applied as a clip's look or as a file's Camera Log. See [Color grading](color-grading.md). |

Caption files (`.srt`) are not media: bring them in with **File ▸ Import Captions…**. See [Captions](captions.md).

### Add Media

**File ▸ Add Media…** (⇧⌘I), or the Media tab's **Add Media…** button, opens a panel for one or more files. Every file is checked first. The readable ones are added to the Media tab together as one undo step ("Add Media", or "Add 3 Media Files"). A file that cannot be read shows an alert naming it, and the rest are still added. Adding a file that is already in the list changes nothing.

An agent's import never shows this question. Unless you have chosen "always", the file is refused instead.

### Files that are refused

- **A codec this Mac cannot decode** is refused at import with a sentence naming it, for example "*file* is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac." or "*file* is VP9 Profile 1 video, which this Mac cannot decode; VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import." VP8 is refused the same way. A file in a codec this Mac does decode still imports even when some of its data is damaged.
- **A `.cube` the LUT reader cannot read** is refused naming the line and the problem, for example "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65."
- "Could not read *file*." means the file is damaged or not a format Frame Job reads.
- "*file* has no video or audio the app can open." means the file holds neither.
- "Timed out reading *file*." means the check took longer than 30 seconds, usually because the file is on a stalled network volume.

## The Media tab

The inspector's **Media** tab lists every file the project has imported, in a bar, a find band, the list and a footer.

*Agents:* `consolidate_media` (needs a saved project; can take a while and copies as many bytes as the footage weighs).

## Limits

- Consolidate Media needs a saved project.
- Canvas width and height are even numbers from 16 to 16384 px.
- A project holds at most 4,096 clips and 64 tracks (counting those inside nests), 1,024 markers and 1,024 media files, with nests up to 8 deep.
- The Add Media… and Open panels list movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG, HEIC and (Add Media… only) `.cube`. Other sound and picture formats import only by a drop on the Media tab, or through `import_media`.
- `.cube` files are imported, not opened: File ▸ Open… does not take one, and a `.cube` dropped on the window or the Dock is not imported. Use Add Media… or a drop on the Media tab.
- A project file that is damaged or out of range fails to open with a message naming the problem; the package is not rewritten. A package saved by a newer Frame Job reports "project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it". A package with no readable `project.json` reports "*name* does not contain a readable project.json."
# Frame Job

A screencast video editor. A project is a document of tracks and clips that the core edits through ops; the app and the agent both speak in those ops. This glossary holds the terms the spec and the op table use, sharpened as decisions settle them.

## Language

**Op**:
One edit to a project, named by a row of the op table and applied whole. An op the core understood answers one of exactly three ways: it applies and yields a new project, it is an identity, or it is refused. A request the core could not read at all is none of the three — that is a mistake in the asking rather than an answer about the project.
_Avoid_: command, mutation, action (an action is an animation on a clip)

**Identity**:
An op that was understood and had nothing to change: the project already says what was asked, or the op was handed an empty selection. It leaves the project exactly as it was, makes no undo step, and has nothing to explain — a caller told about a rule here would go looking for one it did not break.
_Avoid_: no-op, failure, "nothing happened" (all three hide the difference from a refusal)

**Refusal**:
A rule declining an op, in that rule's own sentence: which track is locked, which clips still show the media, by how many ticks two clips would overlap and how long the shorter one is. Like an identity it leaves the project exactly as it was and makes no undo step; unlike an identity it says why, and it names what a caller could send instead rather than restating the rule. A refusal is not an error — an error is a request that could not be read.
_Avoid_: error, rejection, failure, "invalid"

**Op table**:
The one list of the ops and their arguments, kept by the core and published by it. A row is an op's name and, per **Argument**, its name, its kind and whether it is required — the STRUCTURE of a call and nothing about its meaning, which stays in the prose beside the ops themselves. Everything downstream — the tool catalog an agent reads, the check that compares the two at startup — reads the table rather than restating it, so an argument is written down once and a row that lies is a failing test rather than a call that goes wrong.
_Avoid_: schema, op list, the op enum (the enum is one implementation of the table)

**Argument**:
One named value an **Op** takes, checked against the op table. An argument is part of the CALL: the core knows what it is — ticks, an id, a boolean, a closed vocabulary — and the app says what it is FOR. Distinct from a **Patch**'s keys, which are part of a VALUE and are checked against the property vocabulary instead: `set_video` takes the two arguments `clips` and `patch`, and everything inside that patch is not an argument at all. A name no tool published is not an argument either: it is refused at the door, naming the tool and what it does take, and never dropped.
_Avoid_: parameter, field, key, option

**Patch**:
A partial object a caller writes to say what to change — a clip's property group, a clip's own name and label, or an action's end state. It merges key by key at every depth; a key set to null clears that key, or removes it from an end state; an array replaces the whole list. A key or value the vocabulary does not have is refused by its dotted path, and never dropped, corrected or clamped. The core is the one that reads it, wherever it came from.
_Avoid_: update, delta, diff, replacement

**Selected action**:
The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing, or none. It is view state, like the playhead and the clip selection: not an edit, not undoable, not saved, and not something an agent sets — an agent names an action by its id. It is chosen by clicking the action's band, or by the playhead ENTERING the action's span; it stays chosen when the playhead leaves, and goes when the clip selection changes, on esc, or on the lane's Clip chip. While one is chosen the fields show and write its END state (spec §11 CI-1, CI-2). Actions are numbered by time order.
_Avoid_: current action, active action, "the action under the playhead" (the playhead no longer decides)

**Graphic**:
A clip whose picture is drawn by code: a **Module** in the package's `graphics/` folder, run per frame with the clip's props, rasterized at the graphic's own size. It is a clip's CONTENT, in the place a media file or an image sits — not an effect, and not a plugin: its code reaches no other clip, no timeline, no model and no file, and the same frame with the same props always draws the same pixels (spec §11 G-1, G-5).
_Avoid_: effect, plugin, overlay, template (a template is a graphic someone else wrote)

**Template**:
A **Module** the app ships, which a person copies into their package with Insert ▸ Graphic…: the file is written into `graphics/` under a free name (`lower-third`, then `lower-third-2`) and a clip drawn by it is placed at the playhead. Once copied it is the package's own module — editing it changes no other package, and no later app version reaches it. Its title in the Graphic dialog is its `meta.name`, read by compiling it once when the dialog first opens, else its file name made a title; the menu bar compiles nothing (spec §11 G-16, G-45).
_Avoid_: preset (a preset is stored settings, not code), sample, built-in graphic

**Category**:
The list a **Module** is filed under in the Graphic dialog: its `meta.category`, else Other. Every bundled **Template** has one of Data & Time, Screencast, Social & YouTube and Titles & Text; the package's own modules are all listed under This Project, first, whatever their own category (spec §11 G-45).
_Avoid_: folder, group, tag

**Graphic package**:
A `.fjgraphic` file the Graphic dialog's Export… writes (`export_graphic` for an agent): a stored zip of a `manifest.json`, one **Module** and only the project fonts and assets the engine was seen to draw, measure, fall back to or resolve while drawing the graphic's frames and its `enum`/boolean variants — never one of the app's bundled fonts. Its paths mirror `graphics/`, so a later import is a copy; a file name the zip path cannot hold is stored under a tidied one, the manifest keeping the original. Exporting is not an edit. Frame Job opens one (a Finder double-click, the Graphic dialog's From File…, `import_graphic`) to import it: checked, asked about, and its files copied into the front project's `graphics/` under the manifest's names (spec §11 G-46, G-47).
_Avoid_: graphic archive, bundle, template file (a **Template** ships with the app)

**Error card**:
What a **Graphic** draws in its own box when it cannot draw itself — its **Module** is missing or does not compile, or a frame throws, runs past its budget or will not rasterize: dark red, a bright red border, and the graphic's name, its frame and the first diagnostic with its line and column in white. Never the last good frame, which would hide the error from someone scrubbing. An export never delivers one: it is refused before it starts, or stopped at the frame, with no file left (spec §11 G-8).
_Avoid_: slate (the slate is what a layer with no source at all draws), error frame, placeholder

**Module**:
A graphic's source: one JavaScript ES module exporting `render(frame, props, ctx)`, which returns SVG, and optionally `meta` and `schema`. It is compiled once and drawn many times; the standard library is global and nothing can be imported. Many clips may name one module, as many clips share one media file.
_Avoid_: script, component, file (the file holds the module), plugin

**Revision**:
Which text of a **Module** drew a frame: the SHA-256 of its source's bytes, 64 hex digits. Two identical texts are one revision wherever they came from; an edit to the file is a new revision, and an export pins the revision it started with.
_Avoid_: version (the font and asset set has a version), hash, edit number

**Kept revision**:
An earlier text of a **Module** the app kept, named by its **Revision**: the text a write replaced while the project was open, or the text a delete removed. The last 10 per module live in the package's `graphics/history/<name>/`, never the current text among them, and move with the module when it is renamed. A name with no file but with kept revisions is a deleted module (spec §11 G-27, G-29).
_Avoid_: backup, snapshot, undo step (restoring one is a file write, not undo), version

**Props**:
The values a **Graphic** is drawn with, stored on its clip in the caller's key order — a title, an accent colour, a size. When the op that sets them carries the module's schema, each is checked by its dotted path (`props.accent`) for its type, its range and its options, and a colour is stored as lowercase hex; without one, only its shape. Distinct from a **Patch**, which is what a caller SENDS to change them: a patch's `props` merges into the stored props key by key, and a null in it removes that key (spec §11 G-4, G-12).
_Avoid_: parameters, inputs, settings, variables

===== assistant.md ## Limits
- The assistant works only on the project in its own window, and each window has its own conversation.
- It needs your own Anthropic API key. There is no Frame Job account or relay.
- It can't record the screen, close its window's project, or send audio to the cloud transcriber.
- A tool call that arrives during a drag waits until you release the mouse.
- Stop doesn't cancel an export that has already been queued.
- With compaction off, a long conversation eventually fails until you **Clear** it.
- Changing the key or the model ends every window's conversation.
*Agents:* none. The Assistant is the person's own conversation, and its settings are deliberately out of reach of any tool. An agent drives the same tools directly over [MCP](mcp.md), and is never asked first or refused by the assistant's rules above.
===== audio.md ## Limits
- Volume tops out at 3200 % (about +30 dB). The slider covers 0–400 %; type in the field for more.
- Pan, a clip's or a track's, has no effect on a mono source, and Mix to mono has no effect on a one-channel source.
- Track volume tops out at +12 dB (×4). A track's volume, pan, compressor and limiter can't be animated, and a track has no EQ or other effects of its own yet.
- A track's compressor and limiter are approximate in the preview wherever its clips overlap (a crossfade, a nest's tracks); see [Track compressor and limiter](#track-compressor-and-limiter). A nest's own tracks have none, and scrubbing doesn't hear them.
- Ducking follows a clip's length on the timeline, not voice activity.
- Noise reduction removes steady noise only. It doesn't remove sudden sounds and doesn't gate.
- Voice isolation plays only at normal speed: a clip with a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame plays without it. Two clips cut from one take are isolated separately, and the join between them may differ very slightly.

13:## The pages
4. [Canvas, layers, text and shapes](canvas-and-layers.md) — placing a picture on the canvas, opacity, blend modes, shadows and filters, text, shape, image and background clips, and matte tracks.
5. [Motion, actions and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md) — actions that animate a clip's properties over time, motion presets, and transitions between clips.
6. [Speed, reverse and freeze frames](speed.md) — constant speed, fitting a clip to a length, rate stretch, speed ramps and their presets, reversing and freeze frames.
7. [Audio](audio.md) — clip levels, fades and their shapes, ducking by clip length or by speech, noise reduction, compression, pan, mute and solo, Normalize and Synchronize Audio.
8. [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md) — cutting dead air and filler words out of a spoken recording in one step.
9. [Captions and transcription](captions.md) — importing and exporting captions, and transcribing speech on this Mac or with AssemblyAI into subtitles or word-by-word captions.
10. [The Transcript](transcript.md) — reading what is said in the project as text in the inspector, following it as the video plays, and clicking a word to jump there.
11. [Colour grading](color-grading.md) — the Color tab, wheels, curves, looks and LUTs, adjustment clips and qualifiers, Show Ungraded and the scopes.
12. [HDR and colour management](hdr-and-color.md) — how sources are read, camera log, SDR and HDR (HLG) projects, blending, and HDR and SDR deliverables.
13. [Motion graphics](graphics.md) — graphic clips, the built-in graphics, their properties in the inspector, and bringing in your own.
14. [Vertical and framing](vertical-and-framing.md) — the faces, people and salient regions Frame Job finds in a clip's picture on this Mac, View ▸ Show Subjects, Clip ▸ Follow Subject…, which frames 
15. [Podcasts and several cameras](multicam.md) — cameras on tracks of their own, a program track cut from them, Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker… to cut it from the microphones, and Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸ to 
16. [Screen recording](screen-recording.md) — recording a display or a window with system audio, microphone and click rings, recording a camera on its own or beside the screen, and recording voice-ove
17. [Exporting](export.md) — the export sheet, its formats and settings, presets, the Export Queue, and saving single frames.
18. [The Assistant](assistant.md) — chatting with Claude in the inspector to edit the open project, on your own Anthropic key.
19. [Driving Frame Job from an AI agent (MCP)](mcp.md) — connecting an MCP client such as Claude Code, how calls behave, and every tool.
20. [Settings](settings.md) — the Settings window, updates (Check for Updates… in the downloaded copy), the View choices Frame Job remembers, and where it keeps its files.
21. [Menus and keyboard shortcuts](menus-and-shortcuts.md) — every menu command with its shortcut, and the keys, gestures and context menus that have no menu item.

Writing your own graphic module is covered by the
[graphics API reference](../graphics-api.md).

  ui=['Edit ▸ Undo (⌘Z)', 'Edit ▸ Redo (⇧⌘Z)', 'Edit ▸ Cut (⌘X)', 'Edit ▸ Copy (⌘C)', 'Edit ▸ Paste (⌘V)', 'Edit ▸ Paste Attributes (⌥⌘V)', 'Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties', 'Edit ▸ Duplicate (⌘D)', 'Edit ▸ Delete (⌫)', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete (⌘⌫)', 'Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead', 'Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead', 'Edit ▸ Select All (⌘A)', 'Edit ▸ Select After Playhead (⌥⌘A)', 'Edit ▸ Select All on Track'],
  shortcuts=['⌘Z', '⇧⌘Z', '⌘X', '⌘C', '⌘V', '⌥⌘V', '⌘D', '⌫', '⌘⌫', '⌘A', '⌥⌘A'],
  mcp=['undo', 'redo', 'paste', 'paste_attributes', 'duplicate', 'delete', 'lift_range', 'ripple_delete', 'ripple_delete_range', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'set_selection'],
  details=[
    'Undo (⌘Z): undoes the last edit; the item names it, for example Undo Move Clips or Undo Ripple Delete.',
    'Redo (⇧⌘Z): redoes it, named the same way. Any new edit clears what could be redone.',
    'Cut (⌘X) and Copy (⌘C): need a selection. Cut stops before deleting if the copy failed. A multi-track selection pastes back onto as many lanes; text pasted into another app is a short summary.',
    'Paste (⌘V): pastes clips at the playhead, the earliest there and the others keeping their offsets. Nothing need be selected; needs Frame Job clips on the clipboard. Works between documents, media matched by path. A paste from another app beeps.',
    'Paste Attributes (⌥⌘V): puts the copied clip\'s look onto the selected clips; needs copied clips and a selection. Only the earliest copied clip is read.',
    'Paste Graphic Properties: puts the copied graphic\'s properties onto the selected clips that use the same graphic; needs copied clips and a selected graphic clip. A copied clip that is not a graphic beeps.',
    'Duplicate (⌘D): copies the selected clips and places the copies after them. Needs a selection.',
    'Delete (⌫): removes the selection and leaves a gap. With nothing selected it lifts the In–Out range. With an action selected it removes that action, not its clip. With words selected in the Transcript tab it ripples them out.',
    'Delete is dead while text is being edited and while the curve plot holds a selected point (⌫ deletes the point there).',
    'Ripple Delete (⌘⌫): removes the selection, or the In–Out range when nothing is selected, and closes the gap. Words selected in the Transcript tab go first. Dead while text is being edited.',
    'Insert at Playhead: inserts the file selected in the Media tab, pushing later clips along. One undo step "Insert".',
    'Overwrite at Playhead: places that file over whatever is there. One undo step "Overwrite".',
    'Insert and Overwrite at Playhead are enabled only while a file is selected in the Media tab, and never for a LUT.',
    'Select All (⌘A): selects every clip in the timeline being edited.',
    'Select After Playhead (⌥⌘A): selects every clip that starts at or after the playhead.',
    'Select All on Track: selects every clip on the current track; needs a current track and a timeline with clips, and beeps when the track is empty.',
    'The current track is the track of the first selected clip; with nothing selected it is the front-most track.',
    'Selecting is a view change: it adds no undo step.',
  ], guide=G + '#edit-menu', code=[M + ':219', M + ':222', M + ':224', M + ':227', M + ':231', M + ':234', M + ':242', M + ':245', M + ':254', M + ':257', M + ':260', M + ':263', M + ':267'])

F('ref-menu-edit', 'Edit menu', 'menus', 'edit-menu',

    'Paste Attributes (⌥⌘V): puts the copied clip\'s look onto the selected clips; needs copied clips and a selection. Only the earliest copied clip is read.',

    'Ripple Delete (⌘⌫): removes the selection, or the In–Out range when nothing is selected, and closes the gap. Words selected in the Transcript tab go first. Dead while text is being edited.',

    'Insert and Overwrite at Playhead are enabled only while a file is selected in the Media tab, and never for a LUT.',
    'Select All (⌘A): selects every clip in the timeline being edited.',
    'Select After Playhead (⌥⌘A): selects every clip that starts at or after the playhead.',
    'Select All on Track: selects every clip on the current track; needs a current track and a timeline with clips, and beeps when the track is empty.',
    'The current track is the track of the first selected clip; with nothing selected it is the front-most track.',

F('ref-glossary-editing', 'Glossary: projects and the timeline', 'glossary', 'projects-and-the-timeline',
  'Words for the things you edit.',
  details=[
    'Action: an animation on a clip: a span on its action lane with an end state its properties ease to. See motion/actions.',
    'Adjustment clip: a clip with no picture of its own that grades every track behind it. See color/adjustment-clips.',
    'Canvas: the fixed frame every clip is composited into, and every export starts from its size. See canvas/the-canvas.',
    'Clip: one placed piece on a track: a stretch of a media file, or a text, shape, image, graphic, adjustment or nest clip. See getting-started/core-concepts.',
    'Current track: the track of the first selected clip, or with nothing selected the front-most track. See reference/menus.',
    'Edit point: a clip\'s start or end, where ↑ and ↓ stop. See timeline/move-the-playhead.',
    'Frame grid: the frames of the project\'s rate, which every time lands on. See getting-started/core-concepts.',
    'Identity: an edit that was understood and had nothing to change; it makes no undo step and says nothing. See getting-started/refused-edits.',
    'In–Out range: the span set with I and O, which many commands act on. See timeline/in-out-range.',
    'Linked pair: a picture clip and its detached sound, which move, split and ripple together. See audio/detach-and-attach.',
    'Media: a file the project has imported, listed in the Media tab; clips refer to it. See projects/media-tab.',
    'Nest: a clip that wraps other clips into a timeline of its own. See editing/nests.',
    'Package: a .framejob project, a folder the Finder shows as one file. See reference/framejob-package.',
    'Playhead: the current time on the timeline. See timeline/ruler-and-playhead.',
    'Refusal: a rule declining an edit, in that rule\'s own sentence; nothing changes and no undo step is made. See getting-started/refused-edits.',
    'Ripple: an edit that closes the gap it leaves by moving later clips along. See editing/delete-clips.',
    'Selected action: the one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing; while chosen, fields show and write its end state. See motion/select-an-action.',
    'Tick: Frame Job\'s unit of time, 600,000 to the second, which divides every common frame duration exactly. Refusals and agents speak in ticks. See mcp/units-and-ids.',
    'Track: a lane of clips; the front track is the top lane and is drawn over those behind it. See timeline/tracks.',
  ], code=['core/src/time.rs:1', 'CONTEXT.md:1'])

F('ref-glossary-picture-sound', 'Glossary: picture and sound', 'glossary', 'picture-and-sound',
  'Words for what is drawn and heard.',
  details=[
    'Camera Log: a file\'s setting saying which camera log curve it holds, so it is converted at the start of the picture. See hdr/camera-log.',

    'Cutout: a clip with Remove Background on. See effects/remove-background.',
    'Deep: more than 8 bits a component. See hdr/precision.',
    'Dynamic range: whether the project works in SDR or HDR (HLG). See hdr/dynamic-range.',

    'J-cut and L-cut: the sound of a linked pair starting before, or ending after, its picture. See audio/j-and-l-cuts.',
    'Look: a built-in grade or a .cube LUT on a clip. See color/looks.',
    'LUFS: the unit of loudness. See audio/normalize.',
    'LUT: a colour lookup table in a .cube file. See color/luts.',
    'Matte: a track that cuts the track behind it by its alpha or brightness. See canvas/matte-tracks.',
    'Plate: a clip that fills the canvas behind everything, such as a solid colour or a picture from Add Background. See canvas/backgrounds.',
    'Qualifier: an adjustment clip\'s pick of the pixels it grades, by hue, saturation and brightness. See color/qualifiers.',
    'Ramp: a speed change over time, a Speed action on the action lane. See speed/speed-ramps.',
    'Scopes: the waveform, parade, vectorscope and histogram beside the preview. See color/scopes.',
    'Slate: what a clip draws in place of a picture it does not have, such as missing media. See projects/relink-media.',
    'Stem: one track\'s sound written as its own file beside the mix. See export/stems.',
    'Transition: the change from one clip to the next across their overlap on one track. See motion/transitions.',
  ], code=['CONTEXT.md:1'])

F('ref-settings-window', 'The Settings window', 'settings', 'opening-settings',
  'One window, opened with Frame Job ▸ Settings… (⌘,), holds what belongs to you rather than to a project, in four sections: MCP, Assistant, Transcription and Playback.',
  ui=['Frame Job ▸ Settings… (⌘,)', 'Assistant tab ▸ Open Settings…'], shortcuts=['⌘,'],
  details=[
    'It works with or without a project open, so you can set keys from the Welcome window before you make anything. It is a window, not a sheet: the same settings whichever project is open.',
    'It is one window, not tabs: four sections, top to bottom, MCP, Assistant, Transcription, Playback.',
    'Lenses disagreed on the order; the code stacks mcpPane, assistantPane, transcriptionPane, playbackPane (SettingsWindowController.swift:228).',
    'On a short screen the window stops at the screen\'s height and scrolls.',
    'Closing it loses nothing: every control saves as you use it, or when you press its Save button.',
    'While it is open it is listed in the Window menu, so you can bring it back from behind other windows.',
    'The Assistant tab opens it for you: with no Anthropic key it shows "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and an Open Settings… button.',
    'The Generate Captions sheet only tells you where to go: with AssemblyAI chosen and no key, the note under its button and Generate\'s tooltip read "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription."',
    'What each key turns on is on getting-started/ai-and-your-keys.',
  ], guide=S + '#opening-settings', code=[SW + ':110', SW + ':228', 'app/Sources/AppDelegate+Menus.swift:109'])

F('ref-settings-info-buttons', 'The ⓘ buttons', 'settings', 'the-info-buttons',
  'The Assistant, Transcription and Playback headings each carry an ⓘ that explains the section.',
  ui=['Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ ⓘ beside a heading'],
  details=[
    'Rest the pointer on it for a moment (about a third of a second, 0.35 s) to see the explanation; moving away closes one opened by hover.',
    'Click it to keep the explanation open; click again, click anywhere else, press Escape or close the window to end it.',
    'VoiceOver reads "About <section>"; Space presses it under keyboard navigation.',
    'The MCP section has no ⓘ: its text is shown in full.',
  ], guide=S + '#opening-settings', code=['app/Sources/SettingsInfoButton.swift:14'])

F('ref-settings-mcp', 'Settings: MCP', 'settings', 'mcp',
  'Tells an MCP client such as Claude Code how to reach Frame Job, shows the helper\'s path and copies the command that registers it.',
  ui=['Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ MCP', 'Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ MCP ▸ Copy MCP Command'],
  details=[
    'Text, in full: clients use framejob-mcp, a helper inside this app, over a local socket that only programs you run can open; if Frame Job isn\'t running, the first tool call opens it in the background.',
    'The full path of the framejob-mcp helper inside the copy you are running, selectable so you can copy it.',
    'Copy MCP Command: puts the Claude Code registration line on the clipboard, with the path filled in and quoted for the shell: claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- \'/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp\'.',

    'The path is always the one for the app you opened Settings from, so copy the command again if you move Frame Job.',

F('ref-settings-assistant', 'Settings: Assistant', 'settings', 'assistant',
  'Your Anthropic API key, the model, and two settings for long conversations.',
  ui=['Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant'], requires=['anthropic-key'],
  details=[
    'Anthropic API key: a secure field. Paste a key and press Save or Return. Default none.',
    'Save: stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps.',
    'Remove: deletes the stored key; disabled when no key is stored.',

The number can be 20,000 to 900,000; outside that it beeps and the field goes back to the stored number. Untick to never compact. The field is enabled only while the box is ticked.',
    'Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens: lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees, even partway through a turn, never tool search results. Default off.',

    'Saving or removing the key, or changing the model, ends the conversation in every open window\'s Assistant tab; the next message starts a new one. Pressing Return in Model without changing what it resolves to ends nothing.',

F('ref-settings-playback', 'Settings: Playback', 'settings', 'playback',

import re, os, sys, json, collections
from load import load, claims, B
import feats_b
from feats_a import FE

R = load()
c, r = claims()
ids = {f['id']: f for f in FE}
assert len(ids) == len(FE)
assign = collections.defaultdict(set)      # raw -> feature ids
reject = {}
def put(fid, *raws):
    assert fid in ids, fid
    for x in raws:
        assert x in R, x
        assign[x].add(fid)
def rng(prefix, spec):
    out = []
    width = 3
    for a in spec:
        if isinstance(a, tuple):
            out += [f'{prefix}-{i:0{width}d}' for i in range(a[0], a[1] + 1)]
        else:
            out.append(f'{prefix}-{a:0{width}d}')
    return out

AREA2SEC = dict(export='export', recording='recording', captions='captions', cleanup='cleanup', framing='framing',
    multicam='multicam', speed='speed', audio='audio', graphics='graphics', canvas='canvas', hdr='hdr', media='projects',
    motion='motion', transitions='motion', effects='effects', color='color', transcript='captions', mattes='canvas',
    projects='projects', timeline='timeline', editing='editing', playback='timeline', mcp='mcp', assistant='assistant',
    interface='getting-started', settings='getting-started', other='getting-started')
def sec_of(i):
    others = sorted(set(s for s, _ in c.get(i, []) if s != 'reference'))
    if others:
        return others[0]
    return AREA2SEC[R[i]['area']]

def menu_feature(text, name=''):
    t = text
    top = t.split(' ▸')[0].strip()
    item = t.split('▸', 1)[1] if '▸' in t else t
    if top == 'Frame Job': return 'ref-menu-frame-job'
    if top == 'File':
        if re.search(r'Export Captions|Add Media|Caption|Consolidate|Graphic|Font|Add Image', item): return 'ref-menu-file-media'
        if re.search(r'Export|Save Frame', item): return 'ref-menu-file-export'
        return 'ref-menu-file-projects'
    if top == 'Edit': return 'ref-menu-edit'
    if top == 'Insert': return 'ref-menu-insert'
    if top == 'Track': return 'ref-menu-track'
    if top == 'Mark': return 'ref-menu-mark'
    if top == 'View':
        if re.search(r'Preview|Show |Scopes|Loudness', item): return 'ref-menu-view-preview'
        return 'ref-menu-view-canvas-panes'
    if top == 'Window': return 'ref-menu-window'
    if top == 'Help': return 'ref-menu-help'
    if top == 'Clip':
        for pat, fid in [
            (r'Transition', 'ref-clip-transition'), (r'Motion', 'ref-clip-motion'), (r'Look', 'ref-clip-look'),
            (r'Label|Rename', 'ref-clip-rename-label'), (r'Nest|nest', 'ref-clip-nest'),
            (r'Camera Layout', 'ref-clip-camera-layout'), (r'Switch Angle|Covering', 'ref-clip-switch-angle'),
            (r'Add Background|Blurred', 'ref-clip-background'), (r'Remove Background', 'ref-clip-remove-background'),
            (r'Silences|Filler', 'ref-clip-cleanup'),
            (r'Split|Trim|Freeze|Close Gap', 'ref-clip-cut'),
            (r'Detach|Attach|Normalize|Enhance|Match Audio|Synchronize|Switch by Speaker', 'ref-clip-audio'),
            (r'Add Action|Auto Zoom|Follow|Shortcut|Typing|Speed|Retime', 'ref-clip-automation')]:
            if re.search(pat, item): return fid
        return 'ref-clip-order'
    return None

def heading(x):
    m = re.search(r'\((.*)\)\s*$', x['evidence'])
    return m.group(1) if m else ''

def timeline_gesture(x):
    s = x['name'] + ' ' + ' '.join(x.get('ui') or []) + ' ' + x['what']
    for pat, fid in [
        (r'[Ss]nap', 'ref-gest-snapping'),
        (r'Volume line|volume line|Fade handle|fade handle', 'ref-gest-sound'),
        (r'[Aa]ction band|Action', 'ref-gest-actions'),
        (r'Ruler|Marker|marker', 'ref-gest-ruler'),
        (r'[Tt]rack header|Header|header', 'ref-gest-track-headers'),
        (r'Pinch|[Zz]oom|Scroll|scroll', 'ref-gest-zoom-scroll'),
        (r'Slip|Roll|[Rr]ate stretch|edge|Trim', 'ref-gest-trim'),
        (r'Double-click|Breadcrumb|breadcrumb', 'ref-gest-names-gaps'),
        (r'[Mm]arquee|Click|click|[Ss]elect', 'ref-gest-select'),
        (r'[Dd]rag|[Dd]uplicate|Locked|locked', 'ref-gest-move')]:
        if re.search(pat, s): return fid
    return 'ref-gest-move'

def canvas_gesture(x):
    s = x['name'] + ' ' + ' '.join(x.get('ui') or []) + ' ' + x['what']

def put(fid, *raws):

def rng(prefix, spec):
    out = []
    width = 3
    for a in spec:
        if isinstance(a, tuple):
            out += [f'{prefix}-{i:0{width}d}' for i in range(a[0], a[1] + 1)]

    projects='projects', timeline='timeline', editing='editing', playback='timeline', mcp='mcp', assistant='assistant',
    interface='getting-started', settings='getting-started', other='getting-started')
def sec_of(i):
    others = sorted(set(s for s, _ in c.get(i, []) if s != 'reference'))
    if others:
        return others[0]
    return AREA2SEC[R[i]['area']]

def menu_feature(text, name=''):
    t = text
    top = t.split(' ▸')[0].strip()
    item = t.split('▸', 1)[1] if '▸' in t else t
    if top == 'Frame Job': return 'ref-menu-frame-job'

        if re.search(r'Export Captions|Add Media|Caption|Consolidate|Graphic|Font|Add Image', item): return 'ref-menu-file-media'
        if re.search(r'Export|Save Frame', item): return 'ref-menu-file-export'
        return 'ref-menu-file-projects'

    if top == 'Insert': return 'ref-menu-insert'
    if top == 'Track': return 'ref-menu-track'
    if top == 'Mark': return 'ref-menu-mark'
    if top == 'View':
        if re.search(r'Preview|Show |Scopes|Loudness', item): return 'ref-menu-view-preview'
        return 'ref-menu-view-canvas-panes'
    if top == 'Window': return 'ref-menu-window'
    if top == 'Help': return 'ref-menu-help'
    if top == 'Clip':
        for pat, fid in [
            (r'Transition', 'ref-clip-transition'), (r'Motion', 'ref-clip-motion'), (r'Look', 'ref-clip-look'),
            (r'Label|Rename', 'ref-clip-rename-label'), (r'Nest|nest', 'ref-clip-nest'),

    return None

        (r'[Ss]nap', 'ref-gest-snapping'),

reject = {}
def put(fid, *raws):

    for x in raws:

        assign[x].add(fid)
def rng(prefix, spec):
    out = []
    width = 3
    for a in spec:
        if isinstance(a, tuple):
            out += [f'{prefix}-{i:0{width}d}' for i in range(a[0], a[1] + 1)]
        else:
            out.append(f'{prefix}-{a:0{width}d}')

AREA2SEC = dict(export='export', recording='recording', captions='captions', cleanup='cleanup', framing='framing',
    multicam='multicam', speed='speed', audio='audio', graphics='graphics', canvas='canvas', hdr='hdr', media='projects',
    motion='motion', transitions='motion', effects='effects', color='color', transcript='captions', mattes='canvas',
    projects='projects', timeline='timeline', editing='editing', playback='timeline', mcp='mcp', assistant='assistant',
    interface='getting-started', settings='getting-started', other='getting-started')

    others = sorted(set(s for s, _ in c.get(i, []) if s != 'reference'))
    if others:
        return others[0]
    return AREA2SEC[R[i]['area']]

def menu_feature(text, name=''):
    t = text
    top = t.split(' ▸')[0].strip()
    item = t.split('▸', 1)[1] if '▸' in t else t
    if top == 'Frame Job': return 'ref-menu-frame-job'
    if top == 'File':
        if re.search(r'Export Captions|Add Media|Caption|Consolidate|Graphic|Font|Add Image', item): return 'ref-menu-file-media'
        if re.search(r'Export|Save Frame', item): return 'ref-menu-file-export'
        return 'ref-menu-file-projects'
    if top == 'Edit': return 'ref-menu-edit'
    if top == 'Insert': return 'ref-menu-insert'
    if top == 'Track': return 'ref-menu-track'
    if top == 'Mark': return 'ref-menu-mark'
    if top == 'View':
        if re.search(r'Preview|Show |Scopes|Loudness', item): return 'ref-menu-view-preview'
        return 'ref-menu-view-canvas-panes'
    if top == 'Window': return 'ref-menu-window'
    if top == 'Help': return 'ref-menu-help'
    if top == 'Clip':
        for pat, fid in [
            (r'Transition', 'ref-clip-transition'), (r'Motion', 'ref-clip-motion'), (r'Look', 'ref-clip-look'),
            (r'Label|Rename', 'ref-clip-rename-label'), (r'Nest|nest', 'ref-clip-nest'),
            (r'Camera Layout', 'ref-clip-camera-layout'), (r'Switch Angle|Covering', 'ref-clip-switch-angle'),
            (r'Add Background|Blurred', 'ref-clip-background'), (r'Remove Background', 'ref-clip-remove-background'),
            (r'Silences|Filler', 'ref-clip-cleanup'),
            (r'Split|Trim|Freeze|Close Gap', 'ref-clip-cut'),

            (r'Add Action|Auto Zoom|Follow|Shortcut|Typing|Speed|Retime', 'ref-clip-automation')]:

    return None

def heading(x):
    m = re.search(r'\((.*)\)\s*$', x['evidence'])
    return m.group(1) if m else ''

def timeline_gesture(x):
    s = x['name'] + ' ' + ' '.join(x.get('ui') or []) + ' ' + x['what']
    for pat, fid in [
        (r'[Ss]nap', 'ref-gest-snapping'),
        (r'Volume line|volume line|Fade handle|fade handle', 'ref-gest-sound'),
        (r'[Aa]ction band|Action', 'ref-gest-actions'),
